Formulation:
Predisposing: Chronic medical conditions (T2DM, hypertension); lifestyle factors (alcohol, smoking).  
Precipitating: Acute viral illness causing physical discomfort, sleep disturbance.  
Perpetuating: Ongoing physical symptoms, possible work and home stressors.  
Protective: Supportive spouse; employment; proactive help-seeking; no mental health history disclosed.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): “Get back to feeling normal/healthy; stop feeling run-down.”  
- Clinical Goal(s): Monitor psychological impact of acute illness; screen for mood or anxiety symptoms if physical symptoms persist >2 weeks.  
- Actions (Patient): Rest, maintain hydration, follow GP advice on antibiotics, monitor mood, report any persistent low mood or anxiety.  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide psycho-education on mind–body link; schedule follow-up in 1–2 weeks to reassess physical recovery and mood; consider brief screening (PHQ-9, GAD-7) if concerns arise.  

Secondary Problem: Mild situational stress
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce stress related to illness and daily life.  
- Clinical Goal(s): Teach basic stress-management strategies.  
- Actions (Patient): Practice relaxation (deep breathing, short walks), limit alcohol during recovery, continue smoking reduction.  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Offer written resources on stress reduction; reinforce smoking-cessation supports; consider referral to brief counselling if stress escalates.  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Relationship between physical illness and mood; importance of rest, hydration, gradual return to routine; when to seek urgent help (worsening breathlessness, persistent low mood, suicidal thoughts).  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Ongoing fatigue, low mood, anhedonia, escalating alcohol use, return to heavier smoking.  
- Coping Strategies: Relaxation techniques, pacing activities, supportive conversation with spouse, maintain social contact, follow medical advice.

- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded  
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None currently  
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable  
- Review Date: Within 1–2 weeks or sooner if mental health concerns emerge
